GHANA ACCOUNTABILITY FOR LEARNING OUTCOMES PROJECT ADDITIONAL FINANCING 2 (GALOP AF 2)

PROJECT ID: 165557

 

PROCUREMENT OF CONSULTANCY SERVICES (FIRMS)

 

BACKGROUND

The Government of Ghana, under World Bank and Global Partnership for Education (GPE) funding, is supporting the government’s education strategic plan to improve equitable access to quality basic education in Ghana. The Ghana Accountability for Learning Outcomes Project (GALOP), approved for an amount of USD 218.7 million, has the Project Development Objective (PDO) to improve the quality of education in low-performing basic education schools and to strengthen education sector equity and accountability in Ghana. The GALOP was originally implemented over a five-year period from Jan 2020 to Dec 2024. However, the parent project has been extended to close by 31st December 2026 and the Ministry has received a second additional financing (AF 2) totaling $118.8m to scale up successful interventions from the parent project to be implemented by 31st December 2028.

The Project focuses on expanding infrastructure and opportunities for underserved students, strengthening teaching and learning (especially in STEM and competency-based training), modernizing technical and vocational systems, and aligning education outcomes with skills demanded by employers, ultimately helping students transition more successfully into further education or decent work.

Government of Somaliland

  Somali Urban Resilience Project (SURP II)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST(REOI)

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES)

PIU Community Engagement Officer

 

Country: Government of Somaliland

Project ID No: P170922

Project: Somali Urban Resilience Project (SURP-II)

Consultant Service: PIU Community Engagement Officer  

Individual/Firm: Individual

Duty Station: Hargeisa

Deadline: November 05, 2026

Ref: SO-HM-574040-CS-INDV

 

  1. Background of the Project

 

The Hargeisa Local Government is implementing the SURP II Project (Nagaad Project) financed by the World Bank. The Project Development Objective (PDO) of the Nagaad Project is to strengthen the public service delivery capacity of local governments, expand access to climate-resilient urban infrastructure and services, and enable an immediate and effective response to eligible crises or emergencies in targeted areas.

 

Hargeisa Municipality is responsible for managing and supervising all project activities within the municipality, including timely implementation of civil work, procurement of goods and services, application of environmental and social safeguards, and continuous community engagement. It oversees contractors and supervision consultants to ensure quality, manages financial accounts in coordination with the EAFD, ensures timely payments, and prepares periodic plans, budgets, and reports. The PIU Community Engagement Officer also implements the project’s grievance mechanism, monitors and evaluates progress, and regularly reports results and issues to the PCU and World Bank.

Hargeisa Municipality is seeking to use of the SURP II project to finance the recruitment of PIU Community Engagement Officer.

 

  1. Responsibilities

 

The Community Engagement Officer will be responsible for overseeing and facilitating the engagement aspects of the Nagaad Project within Hargeisa Local government, with a primary focus on promoting inclusive, equitable, and participatory processes throughout the project lifecycle. The Officer will ensure that the project is implemented in a socially sensitive manner and that community voices are meaningfully integrated into planning, implementation, and monitoring activities.

  • Provide substantive support in collecting and transcribing relevant information from community members and municipal authorities during field visits and consultations.
  • Keep the Project Coordinator continuously informed about any local issues or social dynamics that may impact project implementation or community relations.

 

All specific duties and responsibilities are detailed in the Terms of Reference (TOR), available on the Hargeisa Municipality website at https://hargeisamunicipality.com or upon request via in-person submission or email.

 

  1. Selection Criteria

 

The selection shall be based on qualifications, experience and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience and competencies include:

  • A university degree in Social Sciences, Gender Studies, Community Development, Public Administration, or another relevant discipline.
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in planning and implementing community engagement activities within development or infrastructure projects.
  • At least 2 years of proven experience in implementing GBV prevention and response initiatives.
  • Demonstrated ability to effectively engage and build trust with diverse community groups, including vulnerable populations.
  • Practical experience in facilitating community consultations, mobilization, and training sessions.
  • Strong communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to manage sensitive discussions with empathy and professionalism.
  • Solid understanding of gender equality, social inclusion, and participatory approaches.
  • Ability to analyze social dynamics, identify risks, and adapt strategies to local contexts
  1. REPORTING

 

The Community Engagement Officer will report directly to the PIU Project Coordinator and work under the overall guidance of the World Bank Task Team Leader(s) for the SURP II Project.

  1. TIMING Duration of Assignment:

The Community Engagement Officer shall be contracted for an initial period of one-year, renewable subject to satisfactory performance evaluation by the Municipality and approval by the World Bank, as well as the availability of project funds.

 

Hargeisa Local Government now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services. Interested consultants must provide the following (i) Curriculum Vitae (CV) with 3 reference people; (ii) copies of certificates of academic qualifications; (iii) cover letter indicating that they are qualified to perform the services and (iv) Passports or ID.

 

  1. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14,3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations. 

 

Interested applicants may obtain further information including a detailed Terms of Reference from the Hargeisa Local Government in person or by e-mail to the address given below during office hours from 9.00 a.m.– 4.00 p.m. Saturday to Thursday.

  1. Background of the Project

 

The Hargeisa Local Government is implementing the SURP II Project (Nagaad Project) financed by the World Bank. The Project Development Objective (PDO) of the Nagaad Project is to strengthen the public service delivery capacity of local governments, expand access to climate-resilient urban infrastructure and services, and enable an immediate and effective response to eligible crises or emergencies in targeted areas.

 

Hargeisa Municipality is responsible for managing and supervising all project activities within the municipality, including timely implementation of civil work, procurement of goods and services, application of environmental and social safeguards, and continuous community engagement. It oversees contractors and supervision consultants to ensure quality, manages financial accounts in coordination with the EAFD, ensures timely payments, and prepares periodic plans, budgets, and reports.

Hargeisa Municipality is seeking to use of the SURP II project to finance the recruitment of PIU M&E Specialist.

 

  1. Responsibilities

 

  • The PIU Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Specialist will be responsible for designing, implementing, and overseeing the monitoring and evaluation framework of the SURP-II project at the city level. The specialist will ensure the collection, analysis, and reporting of high-quality data to support decision-making, track project progress, and assess impact in line with World Bank and Government requirements.
  • Provide substantive support in collecting and transcribing relevant information from community members and municipal authorities during field visits and consultations.
  • Keep the Project Coordinator continuously informed about any local issues or social dynamics that may impact project implementation or community relations.

 

All specific duties and responsibilities are detailed in the Terms of Reference (TOR), available on the Hargeisa Municipality website at https://hargeisamunicipality.com or upon request via in-person submission or email.

 

 

 

  1. Selection Criteria

 

The selection shall be based on qualifications, experience and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience and competencies include:

 

  • A master’s degree in a relevant field such as Project Management, Economics, Statistics, Data Science, Management Information Systems, Development Studies, Social Sciences, or related disciplines, with a focus on monitoring and evaluation, statistics, or research methods.
  • Minimum of seven (7) years of progressive professional experience in monitoring and evaluation, of which at least four (4) years in a lead or specialist M&E role on development projects.
  • At least three (3) years of demonstrated experience in designing and implementing M&E systems for urban infrastructure or urban development projects. This includes results frameworks, indicator definitions, data collection tools, MIS/databases and progress reporting.
  • At least two (2) years of experience on World Bank-financed projects or similar donor-funded urban infrastructure programmes (e.g., AfDB, EU, UN agencies) is highly desirable. Familiarity with World Bank results frameworks and Implementation Status and Results (ISR) reporting is an added advantage.
  • Expertise in survey design, field-testing tools, and use of mobile data collection applications (e.g., ODK, KoboToolbox, ONA) and use of computerized database systems or Monitoring Information Systems (MIS).

 

    1. REPORTING

 

The M&E Specialist will report directly to the PIU Project Coordinator and work under the overall guidance of the World Bank Task Team Leader(s) for the SURP II Project.

  1. TIMING Duration of Assignment:

The M&E Specialist shall be contracted for an initial period of one-year, renewable subject to satisfactory performance evaluation by the Municipality and approval by the World Bank, as well as the availability of project funds.

Program Background:

The MASAR Operation is designed to support the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development in addressing foundational bottlenecks in access, quality, and relevance of education, with a dual emphasis on equity and efficiency. The operation aims to strengthen institutional capacity while enabling measurable improvements in learning outcomes and employability, particularly through early childhood education and labor market-aligned technical and vocational education and training (TVET), and digital transformation in education.

The program became effective in 2024, with a total financing envelope of USD 400 million, supported by the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD). It comprises two core components:

  1. Program-for-Results (PforR): the principal financing instrument that disburses against verified achievement of results tied to government reform priorities.
  2. Investment Project Financing (IPF): a complementary technical assistance (TA) component aimed at supporting the implementation of system-strengthening activities and accelerating the achievement of Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs).

MASAR is structured around four interlinked Results Areas (RAs) that are strategically aligned with key education-sector transition points and cross-cutting governance reforms:

  • RA1: Home to School – Expanding Access to Foundational Learning. This includes (i) increasing equitable access to KG2, particularly in under-served districts and refugee-hosting communities; (ii) enhancing the quality of early childhood education through a revised KG1-KG2 curriculum and quality assurance mechanisms; and (iii) improving foundational literacy skills for Grades 1–3 through targeted pedagogical interventions and a comprehensive implementation plan.
  • RA2: School to Work – Increasing Access to Labor Market-Relevant TVET. MASAR seeks to improve the alignment of TVET with private sector needs by institutionalizing public-private partnerships, scaling apprenticeships, and expanding career guidance and employment pathways. It expands access to early learning, strengthens foundational skills, improves graduate employability, strengthens digital skills, technology-enabled learning, and future-ready competencies, and reinforces institutional coherence through evidence-based policymaking.   • Coordinate the preparation, consolidation, and quality assurance of DLR verification evidence, ensuring compliance with agreed verification protocols and readiness for independent verification reviews.
  • Review Verification reports submitted by the verification agency for the DLRs under result area 2.
  • Support monitoring, evaluation, reporting, verification, and learning requirements across TVET-related donor-funded programmes, ensuring timely provision of data, performance information, and evidence in accordance with donor requirements.
  • Support supervision missions, evaluations, audits, verification exercises, and technical assessments by ensuring data readiness and facilitating access to relevant information and stakeholders.
  1. Risk Management and Troubleshooting
  • Identify implementation risks, bottlenecks, and systemic constraints affecting RA2 and the broader TVET portfolio.
  • Provide timely solutions or mitigation measures and engage relevant directorates to resolve issues.
  • Escalate critical challenges to the Operational Program Manager and DCU Deputy Director with clear problem statements and recommended actions.
  1. Knowledge Management and Institutional Strengthening
  • Facilitate knowledge exchange across MoE directorates and donor partners, ensuring that lessons learned, technical guidance, and best practices are captured and shared.
  • Support capacity-building efforts related to TVET programme delivery, labour market alignment, and TVET qualification equivalency systems.
  • Promote institutionalization of MASAR RA2 processes and DCU TVET coordination mechanisms within MoE systems to strengthen long-term sustainability.

Duration and Location

Contract duration is 1 year with possible extension based on performance and availability of funding.

Full-time presence is required. The Senior Coordinator will be based at the Ministry of Education and Human Resource Development, Amman, Jordan

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Education: A bachelor’s degree in Education, Public Policy, TVET, Economics, Development Studies, or a related field. A Master’s degree is preferred, particularly in education policy, international development, or labour market economics.
  • Experience: At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in education sector reform, TVET systems development, programme management, or donor coordination, including at least 5 years in a leadership or coordination role involving multiple stakeholders.
  • Technical Skills: Deep knowledge of TVET systems, governance, qualifications frameworks, and labour market linkages. Strong background in results-based management, including developing work plans, monitoring progress, tracking indicators, and preparing progress reports. Experience with Programme for Results (PforR) or DLI-based programmes is a strong advantage. Familiarity with Jordan’s education sector, TVET system, and the Economic Modernisation Vision is desirable.
  • Stakeholder Engagement and Communication: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with a proven ability to engage and coordinate government officials, development partners, UN agencies, and private-sector stakeholders. Experience in facilitating workshops, leading working groups, and achieving consensus among diverse actors. Fluency in English and Arabic is required.
  • Political Economy and Organisational Skills: Strong political economy awareness with the ability to navigate complex multi-donor environments diplomatically. Self-driven, results-oriented, and capable of managing multiple simultaneous work streams. Demonstrated ability to produce high-quality, decision-ready briefings for senior leadership and meet tight deadlines.

Reporting and Institutional Arrangements

The Senior Coordinator shall report administratively to the MASAR Program Operational Manager maintain a technical reporting line to the DCU Deputy Director for portfolio coordination functions. For day-to-day operations, the Senior Coordinator will work closely with designated focal points in the Ministry of Education and Human Resource Development, the World Bank task team, TVET donor programme teams, and DLR task team leaders as primary counterparts.

Submission 

Interested candidates are invited to submit their resume and any relevant certifications by the deadline specified in the announcement on the Ministry’s website, to the following email address: a.abumtawea@moej.edu.jo
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview.

GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE (GPN)

The Government of Georgia intends to apply for financing from the World Bank towards the cost of Anaklia Regional Gateway and Overland Connectivity Project, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services to be procured under this Project.  

The project will include the following main components:

Component 1: Civil Works (US$ 205 million). This component will finance the design and build of a railway and related infrastructure connecting to the Anaklia Deep-Sea Port. The contract will be implemented in accordance with the “Conditions of Contract for Plant & Design-Build for Electrical & Mechanical Plant & for Building & Engineering Works Designed by the Contractor (“Yellow book”) Second edition 2017, reprinted 2022 with amendments”. The scope of works includes, inter alia, design and construction of embankment, construction/reconstruction of railway stations and related facilities, railway track, superstructure and overhead contact line in the stations, construction of railway track and overhead catenary system on the main line.

Component 2: Consulting Services (US$ 8.5 million). This component will finance the consulting services for supervision of design and build of a railway and related infrastructure connecting to the Anaklia Deep-Sea Port. The primary objectives of the Services are as follows: (i) review the Contractor’s detailed design and verify its compliance with the Employer’s Requirements; (ii) function as the Engineer in administering the works contract and execution of all rights and responsibilities of the Engineer in accordance with the “Conditions of Contract for Plant & Design-Build for Electrical & Mechanical Plant & for Building & Engineering Works Designed by the Contractor (“Yellow book”) Second edition 2017, reprinted 2022 with amendments”; (iii) comprehensive supervision of design activities and works carried out by the Contractor to ensure compliance with the drawings, technical specifications and various stipulations contained in the contract documents, with high standards of quality assurance in supervision and in the execution of works; (iv) advise the Client on all matters concerning the contract management and support the Client to have the works completed within the stipulated time for completion and budget.

Procurement of contracts under the Project will be conducted through the procedures as specified in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers for Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, dated September 2025, Seventh Edition, and is open to all eligible firms and individuals as defined in the Procurement Regulations[1]. The World Bank shall arrange the publication on its external website of the agreed initial procurement plan and all subsequent updates once it has provided no objection.

CONTRATAÇÃO DE CONSULTOR EM DESENVOLVIMENTO, POPULAÇÃO E POLÍTICAS SOCIAIS

  1. O Instituto Nacional de Estatística (INE) recebeu uma subvenção da Associação Internacional de Desenvolvimento (AID), instituição do Banco Mundial, para a implementação do Projecto Regional de Estatísticas da SADC (PRESADC), e pretende aplicar parte dos fundos para a contratação de um Consultor Individual – Especialista em Desenvolvimento, População e Políticas Sociais, para apoiar a Direcção Nacional de Políticas Económicas e Desenvolvimento (DNPED) do Ministério da Planificação e Desenvolvimento (MPD).
  2. Os serviços de consultoria (“Serviços”) visam apoiar a DNPED na concepção, realização e divulgação de estudos que produzam evidências para a formulação e o aperfeiçoamento da política económica e de desenvolvimento, tendo em conta a dinâmica demográfica, a aceleração da transição demográfica e as condições para o aproveitamento do dividendo demográfico, com recurso prioritário aos dados do Sistema Estatístico Nacional, em co-produção com os técnicos da DNPED e assegurando a transferência de conhecimentos. Mais detalhes sobre os serviços e as responsabilidades da consultoria encontram-se nos Termos de Referência (TdR).
  3. Os requisitos mínimos de qualificação são: Mestrado em Economia, Demografia, Estatística, Economia do Desenvolvimento, Políticas Públicas, Estudos de Desenvolvimento ou área relacionada; mínimo de 8 (oito) anos de experiência profissional relevante em economia do desenvolvimento, demografia, políticas sociais, investigação aplicada ou áreas relacionadas; e domínio da língua portuguesa. Serão ainda avaliados: estudos aplicados em dinâmica, transição e dividendo demográfico; estudos sobre pobreza, desigualdade ou capital humano com microdados de inquéritos; análise quantitativa (Stata, R, Python ou equivalente); notas de política e comunicação a órgãos de decisão; capacitação e transferência de conhecimentos; e experiência em Moçambique, no sector público ou em organizações internacionais.
  4. O Contrato terá duração de 12 (doze) meses, a partir da data de celebração do contrato, com base na DNPED, em Maputo.
  5. Os candidatos interessados e com o perfil requerido deverão submeter os seguintes documentos: Carta de Manifestação de Interesse, assinada; Curriculum Vitae actualizado e assinado, em língua portuguesa; cópias dos diplomas ou certificados de habilitações académicas (graus estrangeiros com a respectiva equivalência); comprovativos da experiência declarada (estudos, relatórios, notas de política, declarações das entidades contratantes ou referências verificáveis); e contactos de três (3) referências profissionais.
  6. As candidaturas deverão ser entregues até às 15:00 horas do dia 05 de Novembro de 2026 no endereço Instituto Nacional de Estatística – Avenida 24 de Julho nº1989, Piso 09- Sala 0901, Cidade de Maputo. Email: presadc.concursos@gmail.com
  7. O consultor será seleccionado de acordo com os procedimentos do Banco Mundial definidos no Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projectos de Investimento, 6.ª edição, Fevereiro de 2025, particularmente os parágrafos 7.36 – 7.37 sobre Selecção de Consultores Individuais. Os interessados devem prestar particular atenção na Secção III, parágrafos 3.15 a 3.17 do mesmo Regulamento, política sobre conflito de interesse. Funcionários públicos e agentes do Estado só poderão ser contratados nas condições e casos excepcionais previstos no referido Regulamento.
  8. Os Termos de Referência e outros detalhes sobre a consultoria poderão ser obtidos no endereço acima e também estão disponíveis em www.ine.gov.mz/concursos. Somente o candidato melhor classificado será convidado para a negociação dos honorários e das condições do contrato.

The Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS) intends to recruit a Sector Coordinator (Senior Statistician) for Administrative Data Production under the Modernizing Ethiopia's Statistical System Project (MESSP) financed by the World Bank. The position will support the implementation of activities related to administrative data harmonization, quality assurance, statistical standards, institutional integration, and the production of official statistics from administrative data sources.

The Sector Coordinator will provide technical leadership and coordination for administrative data production and utilization within Ethiopia's National Statistical System. The successful candidate will work closely with sector ministries, regional bureaus, and development partners to strengthen administrative data systems, improve data quality, enhance institutional coordination, and support the production of high-quality official statistics.

Duty Station: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

Reporting: The consultant will report directly to the Desk Head, Statistics Standard and Quality under the Administrative Data Harmonization, Standard and Quality Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Ethiopian Statistical Service.

Contract Duration: Twelve (12) months, with annual performance-based renewal options up to 2031.

Interested candidates should possess:

  • Master's Degree in Statistics, Economics, Data Science, Demography, Public Policy, Information Systems, or another closely related quantitative discipline. A PhD in a relevant field will be an added advantage.
  • At least ten (10) years of progressively responsible professional experience in official statistics, statistical system development, administrative data systems, data quality management, statistical standards, metadata management, or related areas.
  • Demonstrated experience working with national statistical systems, government institutions, or international development organizations.
  • Experience supporting statistical modernization programs financed by international development partners, including the World Bank, will be an advantage.
  • Strong understanding of international statistical principles, standards, administrative data systems, and best practices.
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate multi-stakeholder technical activities involving government institutions and development partners.
  • Experience in administrative data integration, institutional coordination, data-sharing frameworks, and statistical quality improvement initiatives.
  • Excellent analytical, technical writing, presentation, and communication skills.
  • Proven ability to deliver high-quality technical outputs within agreed timelines.
  • Fluency in written and spoken in Amharic & English.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) can be obtained from the Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS) upon request.

The consultant will be selected using the Selection of Individual Consultants (INDV) method in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

Intitulé de la mission : Recrutement d’un bureau d’études pour réaliser l’étude de faisabilité et l’avant-projet sommaire de deux points d’appui de l’Agence Nationale de Lutte Antiacridienne (ANLA) à Mao et à Djedda

N° de référence PPM / STEP : TD-FSRP2-TD-556939-NC-RFP

Le Gouvernement de la République du Tchad a obtenu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour la mise en œuvre du Programme de Résilience des Systèmes Alimentaires en Afrique de l’Ouest et au Sahel – Tchad (PRSA-TD), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat relatif à la mission ci-dessus.

Dans le cadre de ce programme, l’Agence Nationale de Lutte Antiacridienne (ANLA) bénéficie d’un appui visant à renforcer ses capacités de surveillance, de prospection et de lutte contre le criquet pèlerin. La construction de deux points d’appui à Mao et à Djedda doit permettre d’améliorer le déploiement des équipes, le stockage sécurisé des équipements et pesticides, la maintenance du matériel et la coordination des opérations de terrain.

L’objectif de la mission est de réaliser, pour chacun des deux sites, une étude de faisabilité technique, architecturale, économique, financière, environnementale et sociale, ainsi qu’un avant-projet sommaire (APS), afin de retenir les options d’aménagement et de construction les plus adaptées aux besoins opérationnels de l’ANLA.

Les prestations portent notamment sur le diagnostic des besoins et des sites, les investigations de terrain, le programme architectural et fonctionnel, l’analyse comparative des variantes, l’élaboration des APS, l’évaluation environnementale et sociale préliminaire et l’estimation des coûts d’investissement, d’exploitation et de maintenance. Les livrables comprennent un rapport de démarrage, un rapport de diagnostic et d’investigations, un rapport provisoire de faisabilité et d’APS, puis un rapport final et les fichiers sources. L’APD et le DAO relèvent d’une étape ultérieure.

La durée maximale de la mission est de quarante-cinq (45) jours calendaires, à compter de la date indiquée dans l’ordre de service de démarrage. La mission sera administrée par l’Unité de Coordination Technique et Fiduciaire (UCTF) du PRSA-TD, avec l’appui technique de l’ANLA.

Les Termes de Référence détaillés (TDR) et l’avis de recrutement pour la mission sont à consulter auprès du Secrétariat de l’UCTF du PRSA-TD.

L’UCTF du PRSA-TD invite dès à présent les firmes de consultants admissibles (« Consultants ») à faire part de leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter les Services.

Les critères de sélection d’une liste restreinte sont les suivant :

  • avoir pour activité principale les études d’architecture, de génie civil et d’infrastructures ;
  • justifier d’au moins dix (10) ans d’expérience générale en études de bâtiments et d’infrastructures ;
  • présenter au moins trois (3) missions pertinentes réalisées au cours des dix dernières années, portant sur des études de faisabilité, APS, APD ou dossiers techniques de bâtiments et infrastructures de complexité comparable ;
  • démontrer une expérience pertinente dans la conception d’installations techniques, logistiques, ateliers, entrepôts ou magasins destinés à des produits présentant des risques particuliers ;
  • justifier d’une expérience dans des zones sahéliennes, arides, semi-arides ou présentant des contraintes climatiques et logistiques comparables ;
  • démontrer des capacités techniques, organisationnelles et managériales adaptées, ainsi qu’un dispositif d’assurance qualité.

L’expérience dans des opérations financées par des partenaires techniques et financiers ou exécutées selon des standards internationaux comparables constitue un avantage, sans être une condition éliminatoire. Une expérience exclusivement acquise sur des projets de la Banque mondiale n’est pas exigée.

Les critères d’évaluation, détaillés dans les TDR, sont : domaine principal d’activité et ancienneté (15 points) ; expérience générale en études de bâtiments et d’infrastructures (15 points) ; expériences spécifiques comparables (40 points) ; installations techniques ou stockage à risques (10 points) ; contextes climatiques et logistiques comparables (10 points) ; capacités techniques, organisationnelles, managériales et assurance qualité (10 points).

Le seuil minimal de qualification est fixé à soixante-quinze (75) points sur cent (100). Les firmes atteignant ce seuil seront classées par ordre décroissant de leurs notes. La firme présentant les meilleures qualifications et expériences pertinentes, classée première, sera invitée à soumettre une proposition technique et financière en vue des négociations et, si celles-ci sont concluantes, de la signature du contrat.

Les Consultants peuvent s’associer à d’autres firmes pour renforcer leurs qualifications, en précisant si l’association prend la forme d’un groupement ou d’une sous-traitance. Dans le cas d’un groupement, tous ses membres seront solidairement responsables de l’ensemble du contrat s’ils sont sélectionnés. En cas de groupement, la candidature précisera le chef de file, les membres, la nature de l’association et la répartition envisagée des responsabilités. Les références propres à chaque membre seront appréciées au regard du rôle envisagé pour celui-ci.

Les manifestations d’intérêt comprendront une lettre signée, une présentation de la firme et de son domaine principal d’activité, les documents attestant son existence légale, son organisation et ses capacités techniques et managériales, ses références générales et spécifiques, les attestations de bonne exécution et les documents d’assurance qualité. Les références préciseront l’intitulé de la mission, le client, le pays, les dates, les prestations réalisées et le rôle de la firme, ainsi que, dans la mesure du possible, les coordonnées du client. En cas de groupement, la lettre d’intention ou l’accord de groupement sera joint.

Le personnel clé ne sera pas noté au stade de l’évaluation des manifestations d’intérêt. Les CV détaillés des experts, la méthodologie complète et la proposition financière seront demandés uniquement à la firme classée première, avant les négociations.

La sélection sera effectuée selon la méthode de Sélection Basée sur les Qualifications des Consultants (CQS), conformément au Règlement de passation des marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projets d’investissement de la Banque mondiale, dans l’édition applicable au projet, et au Plan de passation des marchés approuvé dans STEP.

L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes, 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs de FPI » de la Banque mondiale, mis à jour en septembre 2025, 7ème édition (« Règlement de Passation des Marchés »), qui énonce la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d'intérêts.

En outre, veuillez-vous référer aux informations spécifiques sur les conflits d’intérêts liées à cette mission comme énoncés au paragraphe 3.17 du Règlement de Passation des Marchés.

Les Consultants peuvent s'associer à d'autres firmes pour améliorer leurs qualifications, mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l'association prend la forme d’un groupement et/ou d’une sous-traitance. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

REPUBLIC OF UZBEKISTAN

CONNECTIVITY AND TRANSPORT SECTOR IMPROVEMENT PROJECT

 

Project ID: P509487

Assignment Title: Development of a Standard Framework for Public Service Obligation (PSO) Contracts for Passenger Rail Transport in Uzbekistan

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): UZ-CTSIP-1004-CS-QCBS-UTY-PM-02

The Republic of Uzbekistan has applied for financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) of the World Bank Group toward the cost of the Connectivity and Transport Sector Improvement Project (CTSIP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") include the development of a practical and implementable Public Service Obligation (PSO) contract framework for passenger rail transport in Uzbekistan, comprising analytical assessment of PSO applicability; development of service quality standards (SLA/KPI); preparation of a standard PSO contract structure and templates; development of a subsidy calculation methodology and analytical calculator; establishment of monitoring and reporting arrangements; definition of institutional interaction mechanisms; preparation of regulatory proposals; and development of a phased implementation roadmap. The expected duration of the assignment is 9 (nine) months from contract signature.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

JSC “O‘zbekiston temir yo‘llari” (the “Client”) now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. Experience in Tariff and Regulatory Analysis in the Transport Sector: The Consultant shall demonstrate a proven track record of having successfully completed a minimum of two (2) assignments within the past three (3) years, each involving tariff analysis, regulatory reform, or financial sustainability assessment of transport services. At least one (1) such assignment should be in a CIS country. Prior experience on assignments financed by International Financial Institutions (IFIs) is essential. In substantiation of the above, the Firm shall provide verifiable client references for all qualifying assignments.
  2. Economic and Financial Analysis of Socially Significant Transport Services: The Consultant should demonstrate relevant experience in the economic and financial analysis of public transport services, including but not limited to the assessment of cost structures, revenue shortfalls, and the budgetary implications of PSO programs. The Firm shall provide evidence of having successfully completed comparable assignments, with prior experience on IFI-financed engagements considered essential. All qualifying experience shall be substantiated through verifiable client references submitted as part of the Firm's technical proposal.
  3. Legal Expertise in Public Service Contractual Documentation: The Consultant shall demonstrate experience in at least one (1) completed assignment involving the legal drafting of Public Service Obligations (PSO) documents, concession agreements, or equivalent contractual instruments within a CIS or EU country. Demonstrable knowledge of Uzbekistan's civil law framework and public budget legislation is required for the satisfactory performance of this assignment.
  4. Regulatory Reform and Institutional Engagement in Uzbekistan: The Consultant shall demonstrate experience in at least one (1) completed assignment undertaken directly in the Republic of Uzbekistan, encompassing regulatory drafting, policy development, or interagency coordination with national ministries or regulatory authorities. Such experience shall attest to the Firm's capacity to navigate the institutional and legislative environment of Uzbekistan effectively. Experience in the transport sector will be considered an advantage.
  5. Local Expertise and In-Country Presence: The Consultant shall demonstrate an established operational and legal presence in Tashkent, Republic of Uzbekistan. The proposed team shall include qualified in-country experts with full professional proficiency in Uzbek and/or Russian, and with demonstrable familiarity with Uzbekistan's governance structures, institutional arrangements, and public budget frameworks. Such local presence and expertise are considered essential to ensure effective stakeholder engagement and timely delivery of assignment outputs.

(Note: Consultants shall clearly describe relevant assignments, indicating the client, country, duration, scope of services, financing source, and role of the firm, supported by verifiable client references.)

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The shortlist will contain 5 to 8 firms.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.13, 3.15, and 3.16 of the World Bank's “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.
